Studium p16.text: The new becomes old; the unusual becomes common; the frisson of what is charming becomes dull.

transcription.reason: Human transcription of the displayed page supplied by the publisher-authorized Google Books preview; no separate full-text transcription was used.
transcription.original_text: The new becomes old; the unusual becomes common; the frisson of what is charming becomes dull.

Studium p16.alignment: The sentence matches the complete German sentence: the new grows old, the rare becomes common, and the attractive loses its power to stimulate. Barnett renders the plural metaphor of blunted stings as a singular frisson becoming dull; this shift in imagery is disclosed for independent review.

Personally compared German p. 16 and the publisher preview English p. 21. The complete sentence, spelling and punctuation match the print. The progression from new to old, unusual to common, and diminished stimulation is preserved, but plural blunting stings of the charming are recast as a singular frisson becoming dull: the image and emphasis move from stimulus to felt response. This is a substantive imagery nuance, not a literal equivalence. Cambridge identifies Stuart Barnett as translator of the SUNY 2001 work; LOC authority identifies Barnett, born 1960.
